llm_note: Same 100 claims (every third test claim), same BM25 candidates. Pointwise: 100 of the 2000 calls lacked a yes or no log-probability among the top 20 and were scored at the floor. Listwise: 0 identifiers missing over 300 calls (0 calls had to be repaired); 5 of 300 calls returned the input order unchanged. Pairwise: the two orders disagreed on 338 of 850 comparisons (position bias), kept as ties. Seconds are wall time on this laptop with llama-server's prompt cache on (the shared system prompt and claim are reused between calls); the trained rerankers' seconds are one batch of 20 on MPS.
llm_summary: nDCG@10 0.681 pointwise and 0.668 listwise, against 0.743 for the trained reranker and 0.671 for BM25 alone, at about 20.3 and 13.9 seconds per claim against 4.83; pairwise comparisons on 50 claims did best of the three (0.764 against 0.747 for BM25 and 0.782 for Qwen3-Reranker on the same claims, top 10)
root_lat: The root's Pipeline lab timed the same models on 40 other claims (p50): MiniLM 155 ms at K = 30 and 590 ms at K = 100, bge-reranker-v2-m3 2,179 ms and Qwen3-Reranker 6,618 ms at K = 30. The K = 100 MiniLM batch varied most between repeats here (946, 994, 736 ms per-repeat medians).
tr_note: Zero-shot (the MS MARCO model as released, scored in this run): 0.687 on BM25's top 30, 0.702 on the hybrid top 30 (the recorded-score sweep gives 0.687 and 0.702). Fine-tuned with hard negatives: 0.726 and 0.738; with random negatives: 0.734 and 0.750 (means of 2 seeds). Training took about 182 s per run on MPS. Both fine-tunes beat the released model: three minutes of in-domain training bring the 22 M model on the hybrid top 30 level with the 568 M bge-reranker-v2-m3 (0.749), though not with Qwen3-Reranker (0.778). Hard negatives did not beat random ones here. Likely reasons, not tested here: SciFact's labels are sparse, so some BM25 'hard negatives' are unlabelled relevant abstracts (false negatives, which RocketQA-style denoising and teacher scores address), and the MS MARCO starting point already ranks near misses; at one epoch and one learning rate the comparison is tiny.
